title: $5 billion Firmus IPO divides investors after valuation triples in two months
key_facts: Australian data centre operator Firmus is preparing a $5 billion initial public offering, the country's second-largest ever; prospective investors question its surging valuation, citing an 'unproven' track record.
A term sheet seen by Reuters has Firmus pricing shares at A$11 ($7.63) each, an equity valuation of $30.6 billion, nearly triple the $10.5 billion from a fundraising round at the start of August.
Firmus is backed by Blackstone, Nvidia and local firms including Wilson Asset Management and Argo.
Firmus estimates five planned Asia-Pacific data centres plus existing sites in Melbourne and Singapore will generate about $5 billion in annual earnings within five years (Reuters, last month).

Merlon Capital's Kirit Hara says his firm struggles to reach a market value of 'A$40-odd billion' and flags $30 billion of debt; Morningstar's Lochlan Halloway sees hallmarks of a 'boom phase' and debt about six times forecast earnings.
Indicative orders are already above the deal size; bookbuilding begins Tuesday (6 Oct) and trading on the Australian Securities Exchange is due to start on 23 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: As Australian data centre operator Firmus prepares to launch a $5 billion initial public offering, the country's second-largest ever, prospective investors are questioning the firm's surging valuation, citing an "unproven" track record.
That's nearly triple the $10.5 billion valuation it achieved following a fundraising round at the start of August.
Indicative orders from potential investors for the IPO are already above the deal's size, the term sheet said.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are split on whether AI data centre valuations are running ahead of results, in a very large Australian listing.
